answer: Continuous Physical Relay Proof: each identity must maintain a live, low-power radio relay whose signal strength is checked against a random zephyr of nearby nodes, so a distant operator cannot spoof local presence. When the network tests a node, it measures round-trip timing across that vine of neighbors and rejects any identity that cannot answer within the physical propagation limit. An attacker running many identities pays for co-located radios, power, and a gale of synchronized timing hardware per identity, plus the cost of failing physical proximity checks.
